product.minus: A piece someone spent weeks mastering gets removed without warning, and hours of practice go up in smoke. This destroys trust more deeply than any pricing issue.

product.title: MIDI = trust upgrade; microphone = the weak link
product.plus: Direct MIDI connection to a keyboard delivers the best interaction and silences complaints about the app's hearing — it signals a "serious" instrument.

product.title: Feedback that's too harsh or too lenient — both drive learners away
product.minus: Grading either cuts on a correctly played note or accepts obvious wrong notes in a chord. Without an honest middle ground the practice tool loses its point.

product.title: The keyboard-bundle channel: premium arrives with the hardware
product.plus: Premium codes bundled inside a keyboard box bring in motivated beginners who already own an instrument — a ready-made acquisition channel.

product.title: Serious learners need a big screen — the phone is too cramped
product.minus: At home the instrument sits in front of a computer or tablet, but the app lives only on a phone; sheet music on a small screen is impossible to read.

product.title: Sheet music scrolls past the point of no return — too late to read ahead
product.minus: The notation disappears off the edge right when it's needed; the next bar appears too late. This breaks sight-reading on the fly entirely.

product.title: Slowing the tempo and looping a passage — what learners ask for by name
product.minus: Learners are thrown in at full speed; they want to slow down, repeat a hard section themselves, and hear a metronome underneath the demo.

product.title: Forced re-runs of completed material push returning learners away
product.minus: To revisit an old song you must redo the entire tutorial; a learner returning after a break is constantly nudged to "finish" things that are far too easy.

product.title: Falling tiles train reflexes, not musicians
product.minus: Tile games are engaging, but they don't teach music: a catalog full of nameless filler, reaction instead of skill — adults quickly see through the emptiness.

product.title: "Learning alone, at home, without a teacher" — who these learners are and why they stay
product.plus: Adult self-starters and older beginners value the ability to start at home without a live instructor — for them, that freedom is the product.

product.title: One hand alone while the other accompanies — a piano gap
product.minus: Learners enjoy practicing hands separately but ask for the other hand to fill in automatically — and they want chord-free arrangements for simple keyboards.

product.title: A bad tuner breaks strings and breaks trust in the brand
product.minus: A wrong tuner suggestion leads to over-tightening and a snapped string — a painful, emotional failure before the very first lesson.

product.title: Facial likeness is the core job-to-be-done
product.plus: When the features are preserved, people fall in love with the result: "looks natural, doesn't change my features" — that's the reason they stay.
product.minus: Most of the time the face "doesn't look like me": half the avatars are a stranger, and that kills trust instantly.

product.title: Long hair doesn't mean woman: gender keeps breaking
product.minus: The AI reads gender from hairstyle: cut your hair and you become "male"; a boy gets assigned a girl's face. Users explicitly ask for a "choose gender" button.

product.title: Skin lightening and erasure of ethnicity
product.minus: The AI makes dark-skinned people lighter, turning them into "a white woman." For the user this isn't a render bug — it's a refusal to recognize their face.

product.title: Every body gets squeezed into one template: tall and thin
product.minus: Any figure gets rebuilt into a tall model: no curvy option, no average height, no real weight. The body is as personal as the face.

product.title: Professional LinkedIn headshot is a distinct job-to-be-done
product.plus: A ready business portrait — suit jacket and plain grey background — is the most valued feature for working professionals; it's why they download the app in the first place.
product.minus: This feature keeps getting hidden or axed: "they removed the basic LinkedIn headshot" — and the professional walks.

product.title: Multi-photo identity training is the core retention driver
product.plus: Uploading a batch of selfies from different angles produces a consistent face across all generations — that's the reason people stay for a year or more.
product.minus: When this feature gets quietly removed or locked behind an expensive tier, the loyal annual subscriber loses the only reason they were paying.

product.title: Hair-trigger NSFW censorship kills ordinary use cases
product.minus: A dress, a swimsuit, mild cleavage get flagged as "inappropriate" — and an adult user can't do anything. The filter feels like an insult.

product.title: The emotion: "I finally like how I look"
product.plus: This isn't a photo editor — it's a self-esteem machine: "I was very ugly but this app made everything so beautiful," joy on a birthday because you don't look old.

product.title: "Too AI": uncanny valley deforms bodies
product.minus: Seven fingers, three arms, gym bars impaled through the body in fitness and fantasy templates — fun use cases turn into results too embarrassing to share.

product.title: Nostalgia: updates killed the filters people loved
product.minus: Consistently: "it used to be great, now it's garbage." Artistic effects were replaced by a generic face-swap-onto-someone-else's-body — the loyal old audience leaves.

product.title: These apps are built for women — men have almost nothing to choose from
product.minus: The template catalog is almost entirely female; male presets are an afterthought — half the market is underserved and says so plainly.

product.title: Bringing loved ones, pets, and grandkids to life — emotional job-to-be-done
product.plus: Animating photos of grandkids, dogs on a walk, monetizing the video — the app becomes family memory, not a toy.
product.minus: Quality lets people down exactly where it matters most: lip-sync can't track a pet's muzzle, renders take hours — the emotional moment falls apart.

product.title: Face-data safety: photos left before consent was given
product.minus: Photos are uploaded to a server without explicit permission; the app demands access to the full gallery. For users this is a question of trusting the app with their face, not a privacy setting.

product.title: Catfish fear: someone else's body wearing your face
product.minus: Users recognize the risk: your face on a slim stranger's body means deception when meeting offline and a body-image hit for teens. Honest representation is a real positioning fork.

product.title: Fixes photos without surgery — natural retouching
product.plus: Corrects light and skin while keeping your own teeth and features: "fixes exactly what needs fixing," result shown next to the original — minimal and natural.

product.title: Custom prompt vs. the template prison
product.plus: The ability to write your own description and build any scene around your face is why storytellers and creative users stick around for years.
product.minus: When custom text generation is locked behind a paywall or cut altogether — leaving five preset thumbnails — advanced paying users feel robbed.

product.title: Show the result before payment — or there's zero trust
product.minus: This is a strategic signal, not price-grumbling: "if the product is good, we'll pay once we see it; demanding payment first says it isn't." Even one free generation removes half the one-star reviews.
